tb_Unity_Event: UInt16 Id // The unity event: the table number a script starts the unity mode with.
UInt16 DsPoint1 // The D.S points stage 1 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint2 // The D.S points stage 2 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint3 // The D.S points stage 3 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint4 // The D.S points stage 4 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint5 // The D.S points stage 5 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint6 // The D.S points stage 6 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint7 // The D.S points stage 7 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint8 // The D.S points stage 8 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint9 // The D.S points stage 9 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint10 // The D.S points stage 10 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint11 // The D.S points stage 11 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint12 // The D.S points stage 12 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint13 // The D.S points stage 13 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint14 // The D.S points stage 14 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 DsPoint15 // The D.S points stage 15 of the event gives every player standing.
UInt16 BonusRate // The chance, in percent, of the bonus monsters of the event.
tb_Akashic_Make: Int32 Id // The id of the recipe: the id of the card it makes in every row.
Byte MaterialKind // What the main material is: 1 a card (166 rows), 0 an item.
Int32 Material // The main material: a card or an item, by MaterialKind. The client shows it in the window of the recipe.
Int32 Card // An item the recipe also takes (three kinds, all of one item class), 0 for none. The client shows it with the main material.
Byte ExtraCount // How many extra cards the recipe takes, 0 to 2. The client fills that many places for them.
Int32 Gold // The gold the recipe costs. The client compares it with the money of the player.
Int32 Result // The card the recipe makes: the id of the recipe in every row.
tb_Hidden_Event: Int16 Id // The id of the hidden event: the id of the box of the map that starts it.
Int32 Condition1 // A row of tb_Event_Condition the event may ask for, 0 for none.
Int32 Condition2 // A row of tb_Event_Condition the event may ask for, 0 for none.
Int32 Condition3 // A row of tb_Event_Condition the event may ask for, 0 for none.
Int32 Condition4 // A row of tb_Event_Condition the event may ask for, 0 for none.
Int32 Condition5 // A row of tb_Event_Condition the event may ask for, 0 for none.
Int16 Rate1 // The weight of Condition1 when the condition is picked.
Int16 Rate2 // The weight of Condition2 when the condition is picked.
Int16 Rate3 // The weight of Condition3 when the condition is picked.
Int16 Rate4 // The weight of Condition4 when the condition is picked.
Int16 Rate5 // The weight of Condition5 when the condition is picked.
Int32 RewardItem // The item a met event gives. The server's own table gives other items.
Byte RewardCount // How many of the item.
tb_Akashic_Parts: Int16 Id // The id of the row, which tb_Akashic_Records names in its Part columns.
String Model // The model of the card's creature: the client sets it as the model path of the item it builds for the creature.
String Animation // The base path of the creature's animations: the client loads it with .anim and .vTransition.
tb_Skill_Script: Int16 Id // The id of the row, which tb_Skill names in its Script column.
String Name // The name of the skill, shown in the skill window and the tooltip.
String Description // What the skill does, shown in the tooltip.
String LevelText // What this level of the skill gives, shown in the tooltip under its own heading. "." and "LvMax" on many rows.
String Icon // The icon of the skill, a path without the extension (the client adds ".png"). "0" for none.
Int32 ShownSkill1 // A skill whose icon the tooltip shows in a section of its own. 0 in every row of this client, so what the section is for is not settled.
Int32 ShownSkill2 // A second skill shown in that section of the tooltip (see ShownSkill1). 0 in every row of this client.
String DescriptionImage // A picture the skill window shows, a path without the extension (the client adds ".png"). "0" on all but five rows.
tb_Akashic_Records: Int32 Id // The id of the card, which is also its item id in tb_Item (every row).
Int16 Name // The name of the card: a row of tb_UI_String (every row). The client looks the name up there. Ids above 32767 read negative here, as the ids of tb_UI_String do.
Int32 Family // The family of the card: the levels of one card share it, and it is the id without its last two digits on 252 rows. 0 on 46 rows. No client code that reads it was found.
Int16 FamilyName // The name of the family, shared by the levels of a card: a row of tb_UI_String (every row). Ids above 32767 read negative, as in tb_UI_String.
Int16 Position // The place of the card in the book of cards, 0 to 298, one per card. The server keeps a recorded card at this place; no client code that reads it was found.
Byte Type // The kind of card: 1 brings a creature in (a summon card), 4 gives its effect by itself (a passive card); 6 is on three rows and not settled.
Byte // Not known: 1 on 140 cards. The client passes whether it is 1 to the view of a card. The original server's row has a flag of cards sold for cash at this place (every common row agrees).
Byte Rank // The rank of the card, 1 to 3. The client passes it to the view of a card.
Byte RarePoint // The rarity of the card, 1 to 3. The client passes it to the view of a card; the server makes cards only from extras of the same rarity.
Byte // Not known: 1 on 70 cards. The client passes whether it is 1 to the view of a card. The original server's row has a flag of hidden cards at this place (every common row agrees).
String Illustration // The picture of the card, a path under Akashic_Records/Illustration.
String // The same path as Illustration in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
Int16 Part // The row of tb_Akashic_Parts with the model and the animations of the card's creature (every row; the passive cards share 20000 and 30000).
Int16 Part2 // A second row of tb_Akashic_Parts (12 rows). No client code that reads it was found.
Int16 Part3 // A third row of tb_Akashic_Parts (3 rows). No client code that reads it was found.
String CodeName // The name of the creature's effect file (the client loads it under FXs with .XML) and of its action file. "0" on the passive cards.
Int16 ActionGroup // A number of the actions of the creature, on the summon cards only. No client code that reads it was found.
Int32 UseSkill // The skill the player uses to call the card: 30000 on every summon card, 0 on the others. The client starts it when the card is called.
Byte InvokeCondition // When a passive card takes effect: the number of a condition. 0 for a card that does not take effect by itself.
Int16 InvokeRate // The chance a passive card takes effect when its condition is met, out of 10000.
Int32 Buff // What the card does: on a passive card the buff it gives; on a summon card the skill of the creature it brings in. The ids of the two overlap.
Int32 Cooldown // How long the cooldown of the card lasts, in milliseconds.
Int32 CooldownGroup // The cooldown group of the card: calling it starts the cooldown of every card of its group.
Byte // Not known: 2 on all but three rows. The original server's row has a flag about keeping the cooldown at this place, like CooldownSave of tb_Skill.
Int16 CooldownGlobal // The cooldown a summon card puts on every card, in milliseconds (15000 on every summon card).
Int32 Disassemble // The row of tb_Akashic_Disassemble that says what taking the card apart gives: the id of the card itself in every row.
Int32 ExpGiven // The experience the card gives to another card when it is fed to it. The client sums it over the cards put in.
Int32 MakeExp // The experience a card needs before it can be made into the next one. The client shows how much of it a card has. 0 on 132 cards.
Byte // 1 in every row of this client. The original server's row has the highest level of a card at this place.
Int32 // 0 in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
Int32 // 0 in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
Int32 // 0 in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
Int32 // 0 in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
tb_Event_Condition: Int32 Id // The id of the condition.
Int16 Text // The text the window of the event shows for the condition.
Byte Kind // How the condition counts: 1 kills, 2 a number reached, 3 an amount collected, 4 uses, 5 at most so many uses.
Byte Target // What the condition counts: a monster, jumps, gold, the longest combo, items used and so on.
Int32 TargetId // The monster or the item counted, 0 for any.
Int32 Count // How many the condition asks for, or the most it allows.
tb_Buff: UInt16 Id // The id of the buff, 1 to 65535.
Byte AllowedPlaces // Where the buff may be put on someone, as bit flags: 1 anywhere, 2 a maze, 4 a district, 8 a battle zone (the server's rule; no client code that reads it was found).
Byte Kind // 0 a buff, 1 a debuff, 2 a combined one. The client counts the buffs and the debuffs of an actor by it.

UInt16 Effect // What the buff does: 0 changes stats; 111 to 114 burn, poison, shock and bleed; 121 to 126 stun, paralysis, sleep, freeze, charm and confusion; 131 and 132 silence and weakness. The client tests several of these numbers.
UInt16 Group // The group of the buff: an actor carries one buff of a group, and the client finds the slot of a buff by it.
Int32 SuccessRate // The chance the buff lands, out of 10000, before resistances. The client rolls it too. Two rows hold -1.
Byte Grade // The grade of the buff, 0 to 10: on the server a buff replaces another of its group only when its grade is high enough.
Int32 DurationMilliseconds // How long the buff lasts, in milliseconds; 0 for as long as nothing takes it away.
Int32 StandByMilliseconds // How long the buff waits before it begins, in milliseconds. 0 in every row of this client.
Int32 TickMilliseconds // How often the buff acts while it lasts, in milliseconds; 0 for never.
Byte OverlapType // How a second buff of the group counts on the server: 0 adds a part of its time, 1 starts the time again. 2 is on 59 rows and is not settled.
Byte OverlapCount // How many buffs of the group may stack: 1 for one that is only renewed, 0 for one that is never renewed. The client shows the stack up to it.
Byte DeleteType // What does not take the buff away, as bit flags: 1 death, 2 leaving the game (32 rows have both). The client clears the buff on an event whose bit is not set.
String ActionName // The animation the carrier plays while the buff lasts (a stun, a paralysis, running). "0" for none.
UInt16 CallOutBuff // The buff that follows when this one runs out. Three rows have one.
Int32 CallOutSkill // A skill the buff calls when it ends: the client looks it up as a skill when the buff is taken away. 0 in every row of this client.
UInt16 HitCallBuff // A buff called on a hit. 0 in every row of this client; no client code that reads it was found.
UInt16 ChangeBuff // The buff this one turns into when its stack is full. One row has one.
Byte Stat1 // The stat the first value works on (the stat numbers of items and titles), or what it means for the other effects.
Int32 Value1 // The first value of the buff.
Byte Stat2 // The stat the second value works on.
Int32 Value2 // The second value of the buff.
Byte Stat3 // The stat the third value works on.
Int32 Value3 // The third value of the buff.
Int16 StartEffect1 // A visual effect, a row of tb_ResVFX, the client starts on the carrier when the buff lands (692 of 708 values are rows of it). 0 for none.
Int16 EndEffect1 // A visual effect, a row of tb_ResVFX, the client starts on the carrier when the buff is taken away. 0 in every row of this client.
Int16 StartEffect2 // A second effect started when the buff lands (11 rows, all rows of tb_ResVFX).
Int16 EndEffect2 // A second effect started when the buff is taken away. 0 in every row of this client.
Int16 StartEffect3 // A third effect started when the buff lands. 0 in every row of this client.
Int16 EndEffect3 // A third effect started when the buff is taken away. 0 in every row of this client.
String Sound // A sound the client plays at the carrier when the buff lands (Common/Item_Use/HP and the like). "0" for none.
UInt16 Script // The row of tb_Buff_Script with the name, the texts and the icon. The client looks that row up by this column; ids go above 32767 (35000), so it is unsigned. 0 on 140 rows.
Int32 // 0 in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
Byte ShowsLabel // 1 when the client shows the label of the buff's script over the carrier as the buff lands (1048 rows).

Byte // Not known: 1 on all but three rows (52063, 52073 and 52083). After a buff changes, the client lists it in a frame of the actor only when this is 1 or the actor passes a check of its own; not settled further.
tb_Item: Int32 Id // The id of the item.
Int32 Classify // The row of tb_Item_Classify: the kind of the item, where it is kept and how it is used.

Byte // Not known. 3 on weapons and gear, 6 on akashic cards, 2 on blueprints of weapons and gear, 1 on the blueprints of one family of costumes, 0 on the rest. No client code that reads it was found.
Byte Rank // The rank (rarity) of the item, 0 to 6.
Int16 Level // The level of the item itself: repair and upgrade prices count with it.
Int32 SellPrice // What a merchant pays for one.
Int32 Price // What one costs at a merchant.
Int16 Stack // How many fit in one slot.
Byte BindType // When the item is bound to its owner: 0 never, 1 when it is put on, 2 when it is picked up.
Int32 Model // The row of tb_item_model: what the item looks like when worn. 0 for an item that is not worn.
Int32 SubModel // A second row of tb_item_model, on six costume pieces only.
Int32 ScriptItem // The item whose row of tb_item_script gives the name and the icons: the item itself on most rows.
Int16 LevelLimit // The level a character needs to use or wear it.
Byte ClassLimit // The class that may use or wear it. 0 is every class.
Byte SellLimit // Limits on selling and storing: 1, 3, 6 and 7 cannot be sold to a merchant; 4, 5, 6 and 7 cannot be put in the bank.
Byte SubType // A variant inside the kind of use: for the items that raise a fallen player it tells whom they raise.
Byte CostumeSet // Whether the item is a piece of a costume set. 0 in every row of this client.
Int32 CostumeSetId // The row of tb_Item_CostumeSet. 0 in every row of this client.
String SlotDisable // The equipment slots the item closes while it is worn: "0", or thirteen digits, one per slot, 1 for a closed one.
Byte Endurance // The endurance of a new item. 0 for an item that does not wear out.
Byte UseValue // An amount for the use of the item: the fatigue a use gives back, the restore counts a tool takes off.
Int32 PhysicalAttack // Physical attack the item adds. Weapons carry it.
Int32 MagicalAttack // Magical attack the item adds. Set on test rows only.
Int32 PhysicalDefense // Physical defence the item adds. Gear carries it.
Int32 MagicalDefense // Magical defence the item adds. Set on test rows only.
Byte StatClass1 // What option 1 works on: 0 a stat, another value a skill or a function.
Byte StatClass2 // What option 2 works on: 0 a stat, another value a skill or a function.
Byte StatClass3 // What option 3 works on: 0 a stat, another value a skill or a function.
Byte StatClass4 // What option 4 works on: 0 a stat, another value a skill or a function.
Byte StatClass5 // What option 5 works on: 0 a stat, another value a skill or a function.
Int16 StatType1 // The effect of option 1: the number of the stat when the class is 0. 0 ends the list.
Int16 StatType2 // The effect of option 2: the number of the stat when the class is 0. 0 ends the list.
Int16 StatType3 // The effect of option 3: the number of the stat when the class is 0. 0 ends the list.
Int16 StatType4 // The effect of option 4: the number of the stat when the class is 0. 0 ends the list.
Int16 StatType5 // The effect of option 5: the number of the stat when the class is 0. 0 ends the list.
Int32 StatValue1 // The value of option 1.
Int32 StatValue2 // The value of option 2.
Int32 StatValue3 // The value of option 3.
Int32 StatValue4 // The value of option 4.
Int32 StatValue5 // The value of option 5.
Int32 Option // The row of tb_Random_Option: the random stats a new item of this kind is rolled from.
Int32 Socket // The sockets of the item: a short id on weapons, a row of tb_Costume_Socket on costumes.
Int32 SetItem // The row of tb_Item_SetItem: the set this piece belongs to.
Int16 Reinforce // The row of the upgrade table that prices and limits upgrading the item.
Int32 Evolution // The row of tb_Item_Evolution: what the item can evolve into. One row of this client has it.
Int16 Disassemble // The row of tb_Disassemble: what taking the item apart gives.
Int32 Furniture // The furniture of a room this item places, 1 to 547. 0 for an item that is not furniture.
Byte CooldownGroup // The cooldown group: using one item starts the cooldown of every item of its group.
Int32 CooldownMilliseconds // How long the cooldown lasts, in milliseconds.
Byte CooldownSaved // Whether the cooldown is kept over a logout. 0 in every row of this client.
Int16 EffectType // What using the item does: the kind of effect.
Int32 EffectValue // The number the effect works with: a row of another table or an amount, by the kind.
Int16 UseEffect // What the client starts on a player who is told to have used the item (08/13). 0 in every row of this client, so nothing is shown.
Byte Cash // 1 for an item of the cash shop.
Byte UsePeriodType // How the time the item lasts is counted: 0 for an item that does not expire; 1 and 3 are in use.
Int32 UsePeriodValue // The time the item lasts, in minutes.

Byte TuckedLook // 1 on tall boots and on the look of a lower piece made to be worn inside them. When this differs between the shoes and the lower piece of a character, the client draws the lower piece as OtherLookItem.
Int32 OtherLookItem // The same lower piece in its other look (inside boots, or over shoes): an id of tb_Item. Read together with TuckedLook.
Byte SealLimit // How many times the item can be sealed, which makes a bound item free to trade again. 255 is no limit.
Byte RestoreLimit // How many times a broken item can be restored.
tb_Buff_Script: UInt16 Id // The id of the row, which tb_Buff names in its Script column. Ids go above 32767 (35000), so it is unsigned.
String Name // The name of the buff.
String Description // What the buff does, shown in its tooltip.
String Icon // The icon of the buff in the list of buffs of an actor.
String Label // A short label (attack up, health restored) the client shows over the carrier when the buff lands, if its ShowsLabel is 1. "0" on 47 rows.
tb_Defensive_Weapon: Int32 Id // The row: the monster that is the weapon. A weapon is a monster whose kind in tb_Monster is 5.
Int32 Monster // The monster that is the weapon, the same as the row.
String RiderAnimation // The animation of the player on the weapon, by its name in the hero's action file.
tb_Skill: Int32 Id // The id of the skill. 37 ids appear twice in this client's table.
Int16 Script // The row of tb_Skill_Script that gives the name, the texts and the icon. The client looks that row up by this column; every value is a row of it.
Int32 Group // The group the levels of one skill share: for most it is the id of the first level. 0 on most monster skills.
Int32 SwapSkill // The skill this one turns into when the player swaps it (76 rows, every value a skill). 0 for none.
Byte Level // The level of the skill, 1 to 5 (0 on five rows).
Byte UsePosition // 2 for a basic skill every player has without learning it; 1 on the other skills, 0 on four rows.
Byte UseClass // The class that may learn the skill. 0 is every class (and every monster skill).
Byte RequiredLevel // The character level needed to learn this level of the skill.
Byte RequiredPoints // The skill points this level costs to learn. The client compares it with the points the player has.
Byte MaxLevel // The highest level of the skill. The client compares the learned level with it.
Byte RequiredSpentPoints // The skill points the player must have spent before learning it. The client compares it with the spent points; 0 in every row of this client.
Int32 RequiredSkill // A skill that must be learned first. The client checks the player has it; 0 in every row of this client.
Int32 NextLevel // The skill that is the next level of this one. The client walks the levels through it; every value is a skill.
Int32 DivergenceGroup1 // The first group of divergences (branches) the skill can take. 0 for none.
Int32 DivergenceGroup2 // The second group of divergences (branches) the skill can take. 0 for none.
Byte SkipPriorityGroup // The priority of the skill when it cuts another one that plays: the client compares the two. 0 to 6.
Byte SkillType // What kind of skill it is: 1 passive, 2 active, 8 a grab. 0 and 3 to 7 are rare and not settled.
Byte PassiveType // What a passive skill does: 0 for none. 13 gives the buff of PassiveValue.
Byte BehaviorCondition // 46 on the 115 skills of the akashic cards, 0 elsewhere. No client code that reads it was found.

UInt16 PassiveValue // The value a passive skill works with: for the kind that gives a buff, the id of the buff. Buff ids go up to 65535 (115 rows hold 50011 and above), so the column is unsigned, as the client reads it.
Single BasicDamage // A fixed amount of damage the skill adds. The client shows it with AddDamage in the tooltip.
Single AddDamage // A second fixed amount of damage, shown with BasicDamage in the tooltip. 0 in every row of this client.
Single DamageRate // The damage of the skill, in per cent of the attack. The tooltip shows it with a per cent sign.
Single SoulGaugeAbsorb // How much soul gauge a hit of the skill gives back.
Single SuperArmorAttack // How much the skill wears down the super armor of its target.
Byte TargetCount // How many targets one hit of the skill may strike: 15 on almost every row, 50 on 82.
UInt16 MoveSpeed // The speed the user moves at while the skill plays and the player moves: the client takes this value as the speed of the mover then. 22 rows have one (15 to 500).

Byte // Not known: 1 on 50 monster skills, 0 elsewhere. The original server's row has a flag about the state of a monster's target at this place (every common row agrees); no client code that reads it was found.
Byte Attribute // The attribute of the skill: 1 on every row but one.
Byte CostAttribute // What the skill costs: 0 nothing, 2 soul gauge, 3 stamina, 4 soul vapor (1 is health on the server, no row has it).
Int32 Cost // How much of CostAttribute the skill costs.
Byte CostType // 0 the cost is paid once, 1 it is drained for as long as the skill lasts (10 rows).
Byte Direction // 0 in every row of this client.

Byte ControlType // How the player handles the skill: 2 charged, 4 a trap moved with the cursor, 5 charged to the end, 6 marking targets, 8 charged both ways. 0 and 1 are plain skills (the difference is not settled); 7 is not known.
Byte // Not known: 11 on most class skills, 10 and 17 to 23 on others, 0 on monster skills. The original server's row has nothing at this place; no client code that reads it was found.
Byte ChargeCount // How many charge steps the skill has, 0 to 3.
Int32 ChargeTime1 // The time of charge step 1, in milliseconds. For ControlType 6, how long the player may mark targets.
Int32 ChargeTime2 // The time of charge step 2, in milliseconds.
Int32 ChargeTime3 // The time of charge step 3, in milliseconds.
Int32 ChargeTime4 // The time of charge step 4, in milliseconds. 0 in every row of this client.
Int32 // Not known: the client adds it, divided by the charge time, to a running amount while a skill charges. 0 in every row of this client.
Int32 ChargeDistanceMin // How far ahead a charged skill reaches with no charge. The client places the target marker this far ahead and moves it out to ChargeDistanceMax over ChargeTime1.
Int32 ChargeDistanceMax // How far ahead a charged skill reaches when fully charged (see ChargeDistanceMin).
Byte MaxMarkedTargets // For ControlType 6: how many targets the player may mark; the skill goes off when that many are marked. One row has it.
UInt16 RangeMin // The nearest distance the skill is used from. The client reads it unsigned.
UInt16 RangeMax // The farthest distance the skill reaches. The client reads it unsigned; 74 monster skills hold 50000, a reach over the whole map.
Byte Angle // How far, in degrees, the user may look away from its target when the skill starts.
Byte RotationType // 1 when the skill starts whatever way the user looks.
Byte UseState // The state the user must be in to start the skill: 1 any.
Byte NormalState // More states the skill may start in, as bit flags: 4 lying down, 0x10 only under a buff that allows it; 8 is not settled.
Byte NoCollision // 1 when the user passes through others while the skill plays: the client turns the user's collision off at the start and on at the end.
Int32 ChainSkill // The skill the client asks to use next when this one ends. 0 for none; 95 of 101 values are skills of this table.
Int32 Cooldown // How long the cooldown lasts, in milliseconds.
Int32 CooldownGroup // The cooldown group: using the skill starts the cooldown of every skill of its group.
Byte CooldownSave // 2 on the 188 skills of the akashic cards, 0 elsewhere. Whether it keeps the cooldown over a logout is not settled.
Int16 GlobalCooldown // The cooldown the skill puts on every skill, in milliseconds.
String // "0" in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
Int16 // 0 in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
Int32 // 0 in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
Byte BulletSyncType // How the shots of the skill are kept in step: 2 the client flies them itself.
String AnimationStart // The animation the skill starts with.
String AnimationLoop // The animation that loops while the skill is held.
String AnimationExtra // An extra animation, mostly of charging.
String AnimationEnd // The animation the skill ends with (the attack).
Byte KeyPressFollowUp // 1 when pressing the skill's key again while it plays sends the key press to the server (39 rows). One row has 2, which is not known.
Int32 LoopTime // How long the loop animation plays, in milliseconds. 0 lets the animation's own length count.
UInt16 Duration // How long the skill plays, in milliseconds. Three rows hold more than 32767, so the column is unsigned.
Byte // Not known: 1 on 9 skills. The client tests it against the state of the user (1 using a skill, 2 some motions, 3 always) in a check whose use was not found.
Byte // Not known: 1 on 18 skills and 2 on 2. The client keeps it while the skill plays; with 2, a skill used in the air stops its animation.
Int16 // 0 in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
String // "none" in every row of this client. No client code that reads it was found.
String CameraFile // A camera file the client plays when the skill starts (40 rows).
String ChargeMarkerEffect // The effect the client places as the target marker of a charged skill, at the distance of ChargeDistanceMin and ChargeDistanceMax.
Byte // Not known: 1 on the one row with a Movie. When it is 2 the client places the Prefab.
String Movie // A movie the client plays during the skill (one row).
String Prefab // A prefab under World that the client places when column 73 is 2. "0" in every row of this client.
Byte // Not known: 1 on most player skills, 0, 2 and 16 on others. No client code that reads it was found.
Byte // Not known: 1 on 161 skills. While it is 1 the client turns the user to its current facing, as it does under one of its own settings; not followed further.
Byte TargetType // 1 when the skill is for the one who owns the user (a monster's owner), not for its enemy.
Byte // Not known: 1 on 58 skills. The client passes it along when it plays CameraFile, but none of these rows has a camera file.
Byte // Not known: 1 on 3 skills. The client takes another path when such a skill is used; not followed further.
Byte // Not known: 1 and 2 on 38 skills each. When it is not 0 the client sets a state on each of six skill slots holding such a skill; what the state shows is not known.
tb_Make: Int32 Id // The id of the recipe: the id of its blueprint item in tb_Item.
Int32 Group // The first level of the crafting menu, 1 to 5.
Int32 Category // The second level of the crafting menu.
Int32 SubCategory // The third level of the crafting menu.
Int32 Product // The item that is made.
Int32 Product2 // A second item that is made. 0 in every row of this client.
Int32 Product3 // A third item that is made. 0 in every row of this client.
Int32 Material1 // The first material: an item id. It is the blueprint on most rows.
Int32 Material4 // The fourth material. 0 when the recipe takes three.
Int16 MaterialCount1 // How many of the first material.
Int16 MaterialCount2 // How many of the second material.
Int16 MaterialCount3 // How many of the third material.
Int16 MaterialCount4 // How many of the fourth material.
Int16 BattlePoint // A cost in a second currency. 0 in every row of this client, so which currency is not settled.
Int32 Gold // The gold the making costs.
Int16 Priority // The order in the list. 9999 in every row of this client.
